BOXING GRANNIES

By: Nicky Troll | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
You’re never to old to kick some butt and get fit. We meet Cosmo City’s boxing grannies that have jumped into the fitness ring.

Unique Selling Point:
Amusing story feel good story that highlights the important health benefits of senior exercise.

Opportunity for creative visual devices.

Summary:
Gogos packing punches to win the battle against old age. A former body builder with a big soft heart is training grannies between the ages of 60 and 75 – giving them a new lease on life with their new found fitness regimes.

We meet the Grannies and learn about their frustrations and fitness frenzy.

Further information:
Claude Maphosa is a former bodybuilder and the owner of the A-Team gym - a small gym at a community centre in Cosmo City. He got the opportunity of a lifetime to open the gym about four years ago, and noticed that many grannies were visiting… and were surprisingly interested in the boxing! He“Age should never stop you from enjoying what you love,”
Claude believes Gogos are the pillars of communities – and that elders should not only be respected but supported & encouraged as well.

“People often think that because they are old they can’t physically exercise,” he explains, “but boxing is for everyone.” Aside from improving fitness, it acts as a form of therapy. Even for grannies. Those who spend regular time in the ring testify to the sport’s physical and mental rewards. The joy beaming from the faces of his gogos each time they spar is enough to let Maphosa know he’s making a difference.

TRAINING & THE BENEFITS
About 30 gogos train with coach Claude in twice-weekly sessions. They work out life’s frustration while becoming more mobile and improving fitness. While some of grand kids would prefer their grannies to slow down – they will tell you they aren’t quitting any time soon.

Coach Claude’s holistic approach to training not only improves strength & coordination – it makes them feel part of something that is actually good for them! Many claim that they no longer suffer from the ailments they had before and are stronger than ever.

He also ensures that he provides them with a meal at every training session. Grannies hold hands as they pray before taking part in boxing lessons in an attempt to battle old age.

EXPERT INTERVIEW
We interview someone from the Biokenetises Association of South Africa to highlight the importance of exercise in old age and the associated health benefits.
According to the World Healt Organisation - overall, strong evidence demonstrates that compared to less active men and women, older adults who are physically active:
• have lower rates of all-cause mortality, coronary heart disease, high blood pressure, stroke, type 2 diabetes, colon cancer and breast cancer, a higher level of cardiorespiratory and muscular fitness, healthier body mass and composition;
• have a biomarker profile that is more favourable for the prevention of cardiovascular disease, type 2 diabetes and the enhancement of bone health; and
• exhibit higher levels of functional health, a lower risk of falling, and better cognitive function; have reduced risk of moderate and severe functional limitations and role limitations.
http://www.who.int/dietphysicalactivity/factsheet_olderadults/en/


THE GRANNIES
We’ll feature three of these amazing Gogos:

MABLE MAKHOSI, 67-years old
She is engaging and colourful – she battles with diabetes and high blood pressure – she has already seen her reading normalise since she’s become more active.

ZODWA THWALA, 70-years old
She an OLD 70! She is not a poster child for healthy living – but she is precious! Zodwa says while boxing is hard, she loves it and she loves the way it makes her feel – she will not be quitting any time soon.

GLADYS NGWENYA, 77-years old
She’s cute and tiny, but dynamite – She is enthusiastic about her training – and packs the punches – so much so that she ready to dish out a punch if in danger – with a huge smile of course.

We’ll film them at gym training with Coach Claude and then we’ll go home with them – speak to their children / grandkids. Show their daily struggles.

SERIOUS NOTE
Our government provides free health care – they get their meds from state hospitals and clinics – but there is nothing from a preventative perspective offering exercise and fitness. Government doesn’t step in to promote healthy living in a way that is accessible to the elderly. Claude realising the importance of exercise and fitness – even for seniors - sees this as his opportunity to give back, to fill a gap where there isn’t clearly a need and a desire from the gogos to get moving.

Press Release:


Boxing Grannies
Gogos are packing a punch in a bid to win the battle against old age. Twice a week, women between the
ages of 60 and 75, are learning to “float like a butterfly and sting like a bee”, as they train with a former
body builder in Cosmo City. The training is tough and the fitness regimes are exhausting, but it’s giving
these women a new lease on life. Carte Blanche enters the ring with these extraordinary women.

Script:


STRUCTURE

UPSOUND MUSIC & QUICK CUTS OF BOXING

LINK: There aren’t any future Mohammed Ali’s in this ring – but these goggos are throwing punches at old age and they appear to be winning.

VO: Meet MABLE MOKGOSI, she’s 66-years old and PACKING PUNCHES IN HER BATTLE AGAINST diabetes and high blood pressure.

MABEL: it really boxing help me a lot – I tell you truth – that is why I love it. INT1 M9

VO: ZODWA THWALA is a young 75-year old – NOT QUITE THE POSTER CHILD FOR FITNESS – BUT SHE’S A HARD CORE BOXING ENTHUSIAST.

ZODWA: I love boxing very much, what I don’t like is football - I don’t like it but boxing is my favourite.

VO: Then there’s GLADYS NGWENYA, at 77-years old – SHE MIGHT BE TINY, BUT SHE’S DYNAMITE.

GLADYS: I wish I started much younger // I would have been stronger and have muscles .

VO: These are some of the Boxing gogos of Cosmo City, north of Johannesburg. They’ve jumped into the ring to fight the challenges of old age.

NHLANHLA: Is it too little too late?
DOC: No, // the health benefits are still there even if it is just a little bit and you start late in life.

VO: Geriatrician, Dr. Susan Coetzer specialises in medical care for the elderly - she is both amused and amazed by these gogos exercise regime.

DOC: // I think it’s unique and good situation as long as they are not boxing each other lights out

MABEL: but we are not teaching for fighting, even for our family – we just punching to for our health – to move our body, to move our muscles, to make us strong and powerful – you see I can do this, I can do this, I can do this…

VO: That’s of course besides the group’s own little Rocky Balboa – Gogo Zodwa has become fearless with her boxing gloves – ready for any potential danger.

Gogo Zodwa: A thief will never get while I’m holding these things – I’ll hit him without him even knowing. I’ll knock him down and then I’ll hit him with my walking stick.

VO: Some are even ready to throw away their walking sticks. Gogo Gladys had a stroke a few years ago. She says boxing has helped with her recovery dramatically.

GLADYS: I saw the difference when I started, I am less aware of the affects of my stroke, my body isn’t as sore as it was before. I feel boxing is more helpful than the medicine, I feel like I could leave the meds and carry on with the boxing.

DOC: // sometimes medication isn’t even needed later on // In a lot of situations – exercise can help to be preventative – better than just managing illnesses.

VO: The grannies started throwing punches in 2013, when Cosmo City’s community gym was opened by former body builder & personal trainer Claude Maphosa.

CLAUDE: The gogos were always loitering // so they were the first people to notice what is going on here – they were very inquisitive – a gym? And they said can we come join? And I thought they were joking.

VO: But these fiesty gogos were dead serious… soon they were showing up twice a week for training sessions under the watchful eye of Coach Claude.

LINK: Boxing is not just for the superfit - almost anyone can throw a punch – it increases agility and coordination – builds strength and helps to manage stress.

VO: As long as the intensity of the training is controlled and the gogos are monitored – boxing ticks all the fundamental exercise boxes - even for the elderly.

DOC: It ’s a good type of exercise – it involves aerobic exercise, there’s balance exercise as well as strength training, // stretching – so that incorporates all four components of healthy exercise in the elderly.

CLAUDE: //They are stronger than you think – their perseverance and their patience – // these are not ordinary people – they are extra ordinary people – they can do what you think is impossible.

VO: Gogo Zodwa is fully aware of the remarkable transformation her body has experienced as a result of her weekly boxing sessions.

Gogo Zodwa: My whole body ached, my back as well. This part aches, its as if I was beat up but when I came here that all changed I became free.
Nhlanhla : How has the boxing helped you?
Gogo: Zodwa: // I would just sleep, but I don’t sleep anymore I am much better. I am able to do housework, clean and wash blankets - and everything else.

VO: The benefits of exercise is undeniable at any age says Dr Coetzer.

DOC: Even in older adults their muscles have the ability to regenerate and you can reverse illness like pre-frailty if you manage it early enough – you can still reverse it

VO: Something Coach Claude has witnessed himself – he says their fitness improves and they grow stronger every week.

CLAUDE: If I tell you four years back to now – when they were sitting in the door - you thought oh these grannies – but now when they start reflexing and punching – they are totally different.

VO: Gogo Mabel says before taking up boxing, she was very ill and weak. But now, things have changed and even her children have noticed how her health has improved.

MABEL: //The past few years they were so worried in my house they think they will lose me – I was on and off in hospital, they call the ambulance – // but now it’s long time – really I am not lying – it’s truth – it’s a long time I never go there – I just go for check ups.

VO: While she suffers from high blood pressure & diabetes – it’s under control now. Realising it’s a combination of meds, exercise and nutrition - Gogo Mabel also tries to make better food choices.

MABEL: // I just eat the right food – but not all the time, sometimes I find that I haven’t got money to buy it – just sometimes when I got my pension I have to go to shopping to buy my salad that good stuff that I must eat it – but it won’t last the whole month I have to back to mielie pap.

VO: Coach Claude and his team incorporate talks on nutrition, lining the gogos up before training begins for a dose of fresh ginger and garlic to boost their immunity.

He believes the benefits of these boxing sessions go beyond just exercise & nutrition.

CLAUDE: This is more than training for them – they come back they feel good – they feel young again – there is so much that changes within themselves.

LINK: These gogos are the glue that keeps their families together in their communities and while they are respected for their wisdom, they need encouragement and support.

DOC: Exercise helps to maintain your independence it keeps patients functional for longer // the burden of illness can make you more dependent and exercise helps to prevent that.

MABEL: you will see you’ll become stronger – you’re not going to be young, young // you’ll stay strong and healthy you know

VO: There’s no disputing that going to gym and boxing with Coach Claude has given these gogos a new lease on life.

GLADYS: I will never stop, I really, really love Claude. His gym has given me life. I am very happy

CLAUDE: // they are motivating themselves, they don’t get tired – it’s because of what you give them they give you back.

VO: And Gogo Zodwa still has a lot of punches to dish out – she won’t be quitting any time soon.

Gogo Zodwa: I love it, // I don’t worry out earthly things I just focus on this.


PROMOS
PROMO 1
VO: Gogos who “float like a butterfly and sting like a bee”, have taken up boxing in Cosmo City – proving that you’re never too old to get into shape.

ZODWA: I love boxing very much.

PROMO 2
VO: Cosmo City’s Boxing Gogos are smashing perceptions about old age – as they box their way to improved fitness.

CLAUDE: They are stronger than you think – their perseverance and their patience – // these are not ordinary people – they are extra ordinary people INT1 M6 middle

PROMO 3
VO: We meet Cosmo City’s boxing Gogos who’ve jump into the boxing ring in their fight against old age.

MABEL: We just punching to for our health – to move our body, to move our muscles, to make us strong and powerful!

Grannies hold hands as they pray before taking part in boxing lessons in an attempt to battle old age. EXPERT INTERVIEW We interview someone from the Biokenetises Association of South Africa to highlight the importance of exercise in old age and the associated health benefits. According to the World Healt Organisation - overall, strong evidence demonstrates that compared to less active men and women, older adults who are physically active: • have lower rates of all-cause mortality, coronary heart disease, high blood pressure, stroke, type 2 diabetes, colon cancer and breast cancer, a higher level of cardiorespiratory and muscular fitness, healthier body mass and composition; • have a biomarker profile that is more favourable for the prevention of cardiovascular disease, type 2 diabetes and the enhancement of bone health; and • exhibit higher levels of functional health, a lower risk of falling, and better cognitive function; have reduced risk of moderate and severe functional limitations and role limitations. http://www.who.int/dietphysicalactivity/factsheet_olderadults/en/ THE GRANNIES We’ll feature three of these amazing Gogos: MABLE MAKHOSI, 67-years old She is engaging and colourful – she battles with diabetes and high blood pressure – she has already seen her reading normalise since she’s become more active. ZODWA THWALA, 70-years old She an OLD 70! She is not a poster child for healthy living – but she is precious! Zodwa says while boxing is hard, she loves it and she loves the way it makes her feel – she will not be quitting any time soon. GLADYS NGWENYA, 77-years old She’s cute and tiny, but dynamite – She is enthusiastic about her training – and packs the punches – so much so that she ready to dish out a punch if in danger – with a huge smile of course. We’ll film them at gym training with Coach Claude and then we’ll go home with them – speak to their children / grandkids. Show their daily struggles. SERIOUS NOTE Our government provides free health care – they get their meds from state hospitals and clinics – but there is nothing from a preventative perspective offering exercise and fitness. Government doesn’t step in to promote healthy living in a way that is accessible to the elderly. Claude realising the importance of exercise and fitness – even for seniors - sees this as his opportunity to give back, to fill a gap where there isn’t clearly a need and a desire from the gogos to get moving.
